review_role: Ordinary fresh advisory reviewer under rootreviewcarrier-v2; not a scored candidate
grade_basis: Full declared material scientific/recommendation source scope was independently assessed, not stopped after a localized defect. Six material defects prevent PASS. This grade does not attest behavior or historical candidate process.

input_map.authority: Advisory scope/candidate source bindings; not source truth or filesystem firewall

assessment_extent.method: Entire frozen final inventoried; each consequential fact, condition, recommendation, uncertainty, optional lead and check disposition linked to semantically inspected primary sections, or explicitly identified as unsupported/local inference/historical-unverifiable. All mapped identities/hashes were independently checked. Negative statements were restricted to captured content and lexical results were never treated as semantic proof.
not_attested_or_executed: Historical candidate discovery, prior-report permissions and actual candidate source operations (excluded process history).
Original live-response timestamps/headers/status when only body bytes and a selected index claim were supplied.
Live tile endpoint Range/validator/Retry-After capabilities, browser/renderer behavior, actual quotas, crash safety and network behavior (candidate itself proposes them).
All unseen external implementations/deployment versions and broader research universe beyond this bounded declared bundle.
source_text_extent: RFC9111 governing storage/key/age/freshness/stale/validation/directive/application sections and complete-file negative searches.
RFC5861 complete substantive extension, scope, error/window and security text; primary date/status.
RFC9110 governing validator/date/conditional/range/206/304/404/410/416/Retry-After sections and relevant whole-byte searches.
All substantive OSMF policy, rendering-wiki authored text plus raw parser metadata, AWS retry page, Mapbox API page, mod_tile README and leaflet README.

Slippy naming/provider/coordinate/variant/revision sections and whole-byte searches; unrelated coordinate implementation examples were not executed or audited as algorithms because the candidate makes no algorithm-correctness claim.

acquisition.summary: Whole-tile GET plus completed-tile checkpointing remains useful; optional byte resume needs representation safety and a provider-permission gate. Unknown endpoint capability is correctly retained.

refresh.summary: Conditional GET is supported; reconcile successful 304 metadata/pruning with shared event consumers and distinguish unconditional request fallback from full conditional 200 payload.

stale_display.summary: A bounded authorized history/display policy is a legitimate option, but blanket offline cache permission and non-404/410 SIE/removal rules are unsupported.

retention.summary: Keep-one/LRU can be a local choice; quota values/admission remain unresolved. Reconcile successful-validation pruning, storage eligibility/provider constraints and remove the false one-day tile precedent.

six_axis_dispositions.name: All required obligations
six_axis_dispositions.summary: All six obligations have explicit formal coverage, four separate dispositions and eight clustered findings. Material conditions and the cross-topic 304 invariant prevent substantive full satisfaction.

six_axis_dispositions.name: Consequential claims and complete release/default/type/unit/path/authority conditions
six_axis_dispositions.summary: All declared material claims were checked against primary scope. Errors include the wiki parser TTL, SIE status scope and omitted stale/provider/resume conditions. Verified distinctions include AWS opt-in/retry-only versus adaptive admission, HTTP seconds/date versus AWS milliseconds, private/shared TTL precedence, strong/weak validators, source namespace and captured revisions.

six_axis_dispositions.name: Bounded useful discovery, negatives and optional yield
six_axis_dispositions.summary: Useful conditional GET, identity namespace, optional Range, retry analogy, heterogeneous TTL, library limits and joined fixtures were discovered. Correct bounded negatives and optional leads are retained. Numeric tile precedent fails; already-mapped 304 freshening was improperly left as an optional lead.

six_axis_dispositions.name: Wrong rejection, correction and unjustified abstention
six_axis_dispositions.summary: Conservative whole-tile default and rejection of unbounded loops are reasonable; no forced Range adoption or quota value is required. Blanket 404 removal, header-only resume promotion and known SIE-scope abstention are unsupported. The AWS count amendment changes counting method, not source meaning.

six_axis_dispositions.name: Preservation, traceability, uncertainty, options and leads
six_axis_dispositions.summary: Topic-specific endpoint and local-policy uncertainties, source identities, findings, provisional options and leads are present. Primary checking corrects RFC5861 date and semantic attribution; display/history, provider fallback and 304 bindings are incomplete. Accepted keep-1/marker versus unresolved depth/UX are treated as provisional proposals, not falsely resolved product choices.

six_axis_dispositions.name: Proposed versus executed checks
six_axis_dispositions.summary: The candidate clearly labels endpoint probes and behavioral tests unexecuted. Reviewer independently reproduced mapped hashes and lexical results and verified pinned README bindings. Historical candidate operations are not attested by static bytes. Proposed 304/status/Range oracles omit governing conditions; semantic mistakes remain despite matching hashes.

obligation_coverage.text: Give a separate disposition for acquisition and refresh.
Give a separate disposition for stale display and retention.
Identify shared identity/freshness dependencies and reuse invalidation.
Preserve topic-specific uncertainties instead of assuming shared evidence settles both.
Return at most eight distinct material findings across the bundle.
Deliver a bounded topic comparison and discriminating checks, counting shared discovery and synthesis.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: 10 unique documents, 14 predecessor source files, all matching
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: All mapped hashes match in two independent review passes: 23 mapped source copies plus 3 indices. But the original indices contain 6 and 7 documents, hence 13 predecessor files, not 14. Ten unique documents is correct. No unnamed fourteenth file is evidenced; historical candidate hash execution is not proven by reproduction.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Every load-bearing claim was re-spot-checked; captures independently discovered and not merged beyond allowed dependency set
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Indices and unchanged bytes cannot prove search independence, actual spot-check execution, predecessor permissions or discovery process. Predecessor reports and histories were deliberately not read. Scientific statements are independently checked below; these process assertions are not accepted as SourcePASS.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Bounded concurrent whole-tile GET with bundle/region-level resume
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Whole GET and checkpointing completed tiles can be a practical default. Bundle-level checkpointing is an inferred design choice, not a promised HTTP bundle endpoint. Actual concurrency, admission limits and persistence are unresolved; provider permission must gate acquisition.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Raster tiles are approximately 10–40 KB
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: No mapped primary documents or measurements establish this size distribution or universal range. Pixel dimensions and compression formats do not establish transferred bytes. The fallback can be justified by unverified Range support without presenting this number as observed.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Range resumability is optional and disabled until support is probed
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Optionality is correct. A header or successful 206 probe is insufficient for future safe resume; representation identity, validator strength, Content-Range, coding and allowed 200 fallback must be retained.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Accept-Ranges probe gates resume, with 206/416 assertions on a bundle URL
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Accept-Ranges is advisory, not necessary or sufficient. 416 is not resume success and 200 may be legitimate. No captured provider bundle URL exists. A declared test fixture can test these branches, but this probe cannot certify byte-safe resume.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Honor Retry-After and back off on 429/503
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Parse date or nonnegative seconds when present; neither status guarantees the header. Local backoff applies when absent/invalid. RFC 9110 supports 503 timing and RFC 6585 supplies the 429 condition. No endpoint values were observed.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: AWS supplies token quota, exponential backoff and jitter precedent
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: The mechanisms occur in the primary page. This is an analogy, not direct AWS integration or an HTTP requirement. Its opt-in/default applicability, retry-only quota and client scope must not silently become general initial-request admission guarantees.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: The quota halts the acquisition queue
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: A custom queue admission bucket may be chosen, but standard AWS retry quota only prevents retries and never blocks initial requests. The proposed staged check must distinguish initial work from retry work. No executed queue-halting evidence exists.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: OSMF identification, no bulk downloading and cache compliance bound acquisition
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: True conditions are retained in part. The task is offline bundle/region acquisition; policy requires excluding this provider for that feature, not merely bounded rates and app identity. No numeric OSMF rate rule makes prohibited prefetch permissible.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: ETag/If-None-Match preferred, If-Modified-Since fallback with one-second resolution
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Valid general conditional-refresh mechanism. If both validators are present, sending both is normally appropriate; ETag takes evaluation precedence. Last-Modified weakness and nonmonotonic restoration must not become a byte/revision-order guarantee.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: 304 freshens without content payload
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Correct for a suitably matched complete stored response; 304 has no content. Metadata, age and freshness may change even when pixels do not. Counting content bytes is distinct from zero total network traffic.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: 200 replaces entry/validators and demotes old version
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Full 200 response can replace the nominated cached representation, subject to storage eligibility. Demotion, atomic transaction and next-render switching are local proposals, not RFC mandates or executed behavior. Replacement need not imply newly changed bytes.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Full re-download only if no validator was captured
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Sound if it means an unconditional GET fallback when validators are absent. False if it forbids a full payload after a conditional request: changed representations can return 200 despite stored validators. Adjacent 200 replacement suggests the charitable unconditional-request interpretation; not a separate finding.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Refresh outcome feeds display/retention rather than fetch scheduling
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: An event boundary can coordinate the two topics. It does not remove refresh scheduling or freshness metadata duties and requires correct 304 handling.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Bounded SWR is standards-based but windows are client policy because extensions are informational/absent from RFC 9111
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Informational status and absence of literal definitions do not make server-chosen directive windows arbitrary client overrides. SWR requires appropriate permission/scope, or an explicitly separate application policy. Client-selected UX limits can coexist with those conditions.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Show stored tiles whenever offline with an as-of marker; stale use is bounded
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: The offline branch states no age cap and overrides the stated bounded branch. A visible history view may be legitimate under §6, but the candidate cites §4.2.4 for a blanket guarantee and does not define that separate contract. Marker alone does not establish content generation time or remove HTTP cache restrictions.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Any revalidation failure except 404/410 continues SIE display
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: RFC 5861 defines error situations producing 500/502/503/504, not every other 4xx/5xx. Retained upper staleness bound and permission matter. A broader local history fallback is a separate policy requiring explicit classification, not RFC SIE.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Definitive 404/410 means removed tile; refresh terminates entry and display stops
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Stopping display can be an explicit conservative local option; generic 404 is not evidence of definitive removal, and Mapbox documents processing/unpublished 404s. 410 is stronger but still does not require deleting archives. Line 39 applies unconditional status-only termination.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Keep exactly one superseded rollback version until next successful revalidation
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Local rollback depth needs policy justification but is not prohibited by HTTP simply because it is unsourced. A successful 304 is revalidation, yet the declared 304 no-op prevents the stated pruning event. Keep-1 and depth-unresolved labels must be understood as provisional.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Quota with LRU eviction, superseded entries first and in-flight entries protected
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: A quota/LRU proposal is local, not proven library behavior. Protecting partial work is useful, but a hard cap also needs admission/reservation or cancellation rules when protected entries fill it. Values and hard-cap completion remain unresolved, as the candidate says.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: No normative HTTP storage bound; no captured source bounds retention
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: No required keep-N/age/quota number was found in the cited documents. Broadly saying nothing in HTTP governs retention loses storage eligibility/no-store restrictions and application-versus-cache boundaries.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: mod_tile expiry:86400 is a one-day numeric precedent, verified twice
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: 86400 seconds equals one day, and two raw byte matches exist. Both belong to MediaWiki page/parser caching, not tile expiry or mod_tile. The semantic precedent is absent.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: OSMF at-least-seven-days floor binds OSMF endpoints
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: It is a fallback when cache headers cannot be read, not a universal seven-day minimum alongside readable server headers. It concerns allowed local cache revisits, not permission to acquire offline bundles.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Slippy z/x/y identifies placement without content version
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: True of bare coordinate suffix, not of a complete provider URL that may include tileset/revision information. Do not generalize the negative to every URI or provider revision scheme.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Identity must carry layer/style/revision and validators
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Useful namespace separation. Provider/target URI, representation format/@2x and Vary are also relevant conditions. Opaque validators must remain associated with their resource/representation; a separately known ordered revision is not guaranteed. This is a proposal, not an authored universal key schema.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Refresh writes freshness state read by display/retention
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Shared metadata is a real cross-topic dependency. Display may read updated freshness without moving bytes; this is the distinction lost by unconditional 304 untouched assertions.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: 304 leaves display and retention untouched; no-op for both
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Pixels may remain identical; freshness/permission metadata cannot generally be untouched. The local retention rule also expires the rollback slot at the next successful revalidation. A fixture asserting an unrestricted no-op can certify the wrong cross-topic invariant.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: 200 atomically swaps at next render and demotes old version
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: An application transaction is a reasonable local choice. Standards support response replacement, not a demonstrated renderer transaction, rollback slot or crash-safety result. These remain fixture proposals.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Display/retention are read-only consumers and display path makes no network attempt
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Network scheduling can belong to refresh while display consumes state. SWR background refresh must still be coordinated outside the renderer; this does not contradict SWR if interpreted as ownership separation.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Mid-refresh link loss is both a resume/backoff and stale-display event
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: The joined scenario is useful. Whole-tile checkpoint retry and partial byte resume differ, and display eligibility remains conditional. No actual link-loss run was performed.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Conditional re-request should assert 304 and unchanged body hash
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: For a controlled unchanged representation this tests payload reuse. Live requests can legitimately return 200; weak ETag matching does not prove current server byte identity. This test alone misses changed metadata and retention decisions.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Style switch at identical coordinates should not cross-hit
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Good cross-topic identity discriminator. Source/tileset/format/resolution/Vary variants are additional relevant conditions; the proposed single style test is not complete cache-key validation.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Staged 429/503 should honor waiting and quota halting
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Specify absent/invalid Retry-After, date-versus-seconds, retry budget versus admission limit and resource scope. AWS custom millisecond header semantics must not be substituted for standard Retry-After. No such test was executed.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Offline render marker and reconnect refetch test bounds stale behavior
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: It tests a positive fallback path, not window expiry, prohibiting directives, persistent offline age or authorized application history behavior.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Mapbox 12h browser/device versus 5min CDN TTL
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Actual defaults are max-age=43200 seconds and s-maxage=300 seconds. Captured wording says device rather than browser. The browser-exact-phrase claim is false but the tier values are correct. Backend and composite conditions must not be treated as direct freshness guarantees.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: mod_tile computes expiry per tile using a deployment-specific heuristic
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: README says it estimates next rendering and emits configurable HTTP expiry headers. Detailed source algorithm and deployments were not captured; no one-day number follows.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Reject fixed global TTL; adopt stricter client-facing TTL
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Use the applicable per-response private/shared directive and corrected Age, not automatically the smaller of device/CDN numbers. No explicit instruction to use 300 seconds in a private viewer appears, so do not invent that stronger wrong claim. A global local upper bound may still be a design option if scoped and permitted.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Compare Cache-Control/Expires across tiles/regions
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Useful endpoint-specific discovery, with cache class, Age, request variants, backend/CDN and composite conditions. It establishes observations for a capture, not a permanent provider-wide law.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: leaflet.offline supplies storage mechanics, not stale/retention policy
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Offline availability and idb storage intent are supported. The README does not demonstrate implementation eviction mechanics or rule out undocumented implementation behavior. Candidate correctly leaves internals as uncaptured.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Store-aging test should evict superseded versions without deleting in-flight work
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Useful for a future chosen quota/rollback contract. The test cannot establish real storage bounds without filled protected capacity and admission rules; no implementation was run.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: 304/200 fixtures establish one-transaction display plus retention invariants
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: 200 fixture is useful; the published 304 no-op oracle must separate unchanged payload from updated metadata and successful-validation pruning.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Topic 1 is byte movement and topic 2 is display/storage; shared discoveries include 1,2,8 and negative
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Both topics are compared, shared discovery is acknowledged, and finding 8 is labeled synthesis rather than an executed mechanism. These are eight explicit clustered findings, within the material-finding limit.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Topic-1 open items need probes; topic-2 open items are only constants settled by decision
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Both topics have empirical/protocol and policy elements. Acquisition bounds are policy choices; stale eligibility/error scope and actual headers depend on primary contracts and endpoint evidence. SIE standard scope is knowable from the captured RFC, even if a broader application option is undecided.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Cross-topic link-kill avoids duplicate work and sends no display-path request
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: A meaningful future test of ownership and resume granularity. None of the bytes establish actual deduplication or no-network renderer behavior.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: 304 has zero payload bytes and unchanged display/retention
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Zero content is correct. Unchanged pixels need not mean unchanged freshness/display state or retained rollback count.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: 200 new content completion swaps and demotes atomically
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Good explicit new-content fixture; completion and application transaction are to be measured, not inferred from a hash or source citation.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: 404/410 ends refresh entry and stale display, unlike SIE
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Separating SIE statuses is useful; permanent-removal behavior requires provider/local-contract evidence, particularly for 404.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Quota eviction must skip partial/in-flight acquisitions
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Protecting resumable work is a local invariant. A hard bound additionally needs reservation/admission/full-store handling. No observed behavior claimed.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: ETag availability, Range support and Retry-After values remain unknown
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: No live tile endpoint capability calls were made. Standards describe possibilities, not availability of these fields on the chosen provider.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Window/quota constants, rollback value/depth and UX marker remain unknown
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: These are local choices. Keep-1 and marker can be provisional recommendations, but Accepted must not be confused with settled constants or proven need. The offline branch still needs an explicit upper age policy.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Whether SIE governs non-404/410 failures remains unknown
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: The captured RFC settles its own status scope. What remains open is whether the application intentionally offers a differently scoped fallback, under a separate permission/UX contract.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Newer-version existence is unverifiable offline
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Absent a previously captured authoritative revision/update manifest, a disconnected viewer cannot learn unseen origin state. A stored external newer-version notice could alter this; no such input is present. ETag is not a sortable newer-version number.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Reject unbounded loops, default per-tile Range, unbounded stale/retention and fixed global TTL
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Avoiding unbounded behavior and choosing conservative defaults is useful. Optional Range was preserved, not universally rejected. A universal ban on global local TTL caps is not source-mandated; candidate can choose this option. Claimed rejection of unbounded stale use conflicts with its whenever-offline branch.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: AWS retry-quota count corrected from 17 to 15 case-insensitive
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Raw bytes contain 17 case-insensitive occurrences on 15 matching lines. Both counts are reproducible with different methods. Treating this as repaired primary meaning is unjustified, but it is not a distinct material science defect.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Executed hash and keyword spot-checks certify primary checking
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: RFC negatives and most grep-c matching-line counts reproduce. Mapbox browser exact phrase does not occur (device does); 86400 is parser metadata; ETag/Expires/Last-Modified capture contexts are absent from cited vendor/README bytes. Actual candidate execution remains unproven and cannot rescue semantic errors.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Live probes and behavioral tests were proposed, not executed
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Frozen final explicitly labels all endpoint probes and behavior checks unexecuted. Reviewer ran only document retrieval/hash/text/metadata checks. No empirical implementation pass is inferred from these proposals.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: No literal SWR/SIE in RFC 9111; no source embeds revision in bare coordinate identity
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Good bounded negatives. RFC references extension authority; complete provider URLs and validators can distinguish representations, so the identity negative is restricted to bare coordinate naming.
consequential_claim_checks.executed_by_reviewer: Static primary-byte/condition assessment; no behavior test unless explicitly listed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Tile disk usage is redirect rev3082592; leaflet README has no stale/retention policy
consequential_claim_checks.assessment: Both bounded document facts hold. The redirect does not preserve the asserted tile-expiry precedent.

source_evidence.stated_source_facts: Freshness compares lifetime to corrected current age. Shared s-maxage takes precedence only for shared caches; otherwise max-age precedes Expires. Age includes prior cache residency and transit. Freshness does not itself force display reload.

source_evidence.stated_source_facts: Disconnect does not override explicit stale-use prohibitions. Unqualified no-cache requires successful validation; must-revalidate forbids disconnected stale reuse. Applicable shared-cache directives also matter. Explicitly defined cache extensions can modify base behavior, but arbitrary local windows are not automatically such authorization.
source_evidence.basis: Reviewer semantic inspection of hash-bound primary bytes; projections are aids, not independent authorities.

source_evidence.stated_source_facts: Validation sends relevant supplied entity tags and normally Last-Modified when applicable. A full content response must satisfy the request and is storable only subject to §3. 5xx fallback remains subject to stale-use restrictions.

source_evidence.stated_source_facts: Application history and redisplay of already retrieved data need not follow all HTTP cache rules. source_evidence.stated_source_facts: RFC 5861 is Informational, May 2010. SWR is a response directive with a seconds window after staleness; it recommends asynchronous validation and ending stale use when its window expires absent other information. SIE can be a request or response directive, has an upper staleness bound in seconds, and defines error situations yielding 500, 502, 503 or 504.
source_evidence.basis: Reviewer semantic inspection of hash-bound primary bytes; projections are aids, not independent authorities.

source_evidence.stated_source_facts: ETags are opaque, resource-specific validators, possibly weak; they do not encode a universally ordered revision. If-None-Match uses weak comparison and takes precedence over If-Modified-Since. HTTP dates have second resolution and Last-Modified can be weak. GET/HEAD validators can lead to 304, without establishing byte identity for a weak validator.
source_evidence.basis: Reviewer semantic inspection of hash-bound primary bytes; projections are aids, not independent authorities.

source_evidence.stated_source_facts: Range is optional and may be ignored. Accept-Ranges is advisory: absence does not forbid a request and presence does not guarantee future partial responses. source_evidence.stated_source_facts: Ranges address the encoded byte sequence. Clients must inspect Content-Type/Content-Range; invalid or unknown ranges must not be recombined. defects.title: 304 payload reuse is turned into an incorrect shared-state no-op
defects.defect_identity: The cross-topic revalidation event and its published test oracle conflate unchanged content with unchanged freshness/retention state.
defects.source_facts: A suitable 304 freshens a stored response and updates provided headers. Freshness age is measured from generation/validation. The RFC does not mandate an application rollback slot.
defects.materiality: Both topics read the shared freshness state; stale eligibility or validators can change with no payload. The local keep-one-until-next-successful-revalidation rule also contradicts retention untouched on a successful 304. The proposed fixture would approve this inconsistency.
defects.inference: Leaving pixels/body unchanged is valid; metadata and any dependent state are not generally a no-op. Pruning follows the candidate’s chosen rule, not an invented HTTP retention mandate.
defects.limiting_counterargument: The earlier refresh disposition correctly says 304 freshens, and “display” could narrowly mean pixels. The finding concerns the unqualified no-op for both consumers, the explicit retention contradiction, and the missing metadata fixture; it does not claim every 304 must repaint.
defects.discriminating_check: A matched 304 with changed Date/Cache-Control/Expires and an existing rollback slot must reuse content, update eligible metadata/age, recompute display eligibility, and apply whichever successful-validation pruning rule is actually selected.

defects.title: Blanket offline fallback loses HTTP-cache versus application-history conditions and an age bound
defects.defect_identity: The accepted bounded stale policy cites disconnected cache permission as an unconditional offline display permission and treats extension absence/status as client control over directive semantics.
defects.source_facts: RFC 9111 forbids disconnected stale cache reuse under applicable explicit prohibitions. RFC 5861 carries seconds windows and directive scope. RFC 9111 §6 separately allows applications/history to redisplay already retrieved data beyond HTTP freshness. HTTP cache storage eligibility still exists despite absence of numeric retention quotas.
defects.materiality: “Whenever offline” supplies no expiry branch and conflicts with rejecting unbounded stale use. A marker and named policy constants do not define which store is a conforming cache, what permissions apply, or when old pixels stop being displayed.
defects.inference: A permitted local archival/history view is a legitimate option. The defect is failing to name that contract and retaining a false blanket standards justification, not a universal ban on offline display.
defects.limiting_counterargument: Because §6 permits distinct application redisplay, cache MUST rules cannot automatically be imposed on every rendered image. The reviewer explicitly preserves this option and does not force one UI policy or window value.
defects.discriminating_check: Separate ordinary HTTP-cache reuse from an authorized user-visible history view. Test no-cache/must-revalidate/no-store, presence/absence and expiry of SWR/SIE permission, corrected Age, offline age-cap expiry, and the chosen history exception.

defects.title: Provider policy is reduced to rates/identity while offline exclusion and seven-day fallback are omitted
defects.defect_identity: The source-specific acquisition disposition omits the provider eligibility gate for this offline bundle/region use case and generalizes a conditional caching floor.
defects.source_facts: OSMF Standard raster service prohibits offline/prefetch/bulk acquisition beyond actively viewed tiles; it points offline users to self-hosting or explicitly permissive providers. Seven days is a fallback only when cache headers cannot be read. Permitted normal cached revisits are distinct.
defects.materiality: A small, slow or quota-bounded offline download remains prohibited at that endpoint. Applying seven days unconditionally also loses server-header freshness conditions. These are governing conditions of the chosen primary policy.
defects.inference: For this acquisition feature the OSMF endpoint must be excluded or the feature restricted to the policy’s permitted interactive/cache-revisit use. Other providers may permit offline bundles under their own terms.
defects.limiting_counterargument: The final declares no selected live provider. This is a missing conditional source/provider disposition, not proof that an actual forbidden download occurred and not rejection of the generic offline viewer.
defects.discriminating_check: An offline-area request using tile.openstreetmap.org must fail the provider-permission gate. An explicitly permissive/self-hosted provider remains an option. Readable Cache-Control/Expires follow their rules; only header-unreadable OSM caching takes the seven-day fallback.

defects.title: Resume support probes omit the representation binding needed for safe cross-version byte resume
defects.defect_identity: Range capability is used as the enablement gate for resumability without the governing strong-validator, encoded-range and response-branch conditions.
defects.source_facts: Accept-Ranges is advisory; servers may return 200 despite it. Partial pieces may only be combined with the same strong validator. If-Range must not use a weak ETag; Content-Range and content coding/length matter. 416 is an error/length signal, not successful resume.
defects.materiality: The topic explicitly shares changing tile versions. Resuming an old prefix against a newer suffix can corrupt the tile even if 206 support was demonstrated. The suggested 206/416-only oracle misses valid 200 fallback and representation changes. The 10–40 KB rationale has no captured measurement.
defects.inference: Whole-tile retry with completed-tile/region checkpointing remains a sound conservative option. An optional byte-resume route must retain representation binding; no full application plan or numerical optimization threshold is required.
defects.limiting_counterargument: The candidate correctly disables default per-tile Range and leaves live support unresolved. This finding targets the conditions under which its proposed optional branch would be promoted, not a demand to implement Range now.
defects.discriminating_check: Drop a transfer, change origin version, then request the remainder. Strong If-Range/representation binding must select safe full replacement or compatible partial data; validate Content-Range/coding/length and include 200, 206 and 416 cases. Keep checkpointed whole-tile acquisition distinct from an unsupported bundle API.

defects.title: Status-only rules broaden SIE and overstate 404 removal
defects.defect_identity: The bundle maps all non-404/410 failures to SIE while mapping any 404 to definitive removal and leaving already-defined RFC error scope as an unknown.
defects.source_facts: RFC 5861’s defined error situations yield 500/502/503/504 and have a staleness bound. RFC 9110 says 404 may be temporary or undisclosed, while 410 indicates likely permanence. Mapbox documents 404 while a tileset is unpublished/processing.
defects.materiality: The default can continue display for unrelated authorization/request failures and terminate an otherwise useful cached tile on temporary 404. Its status fixture locks in these wrong classifications; “SIE scope unresolved” obscures a condition already in the captured source.
defects.inference: A conservative local stop-on-404 policy is permitted as a choice, and a broader local archival fallback may be chosen separately. Neither should be presented as RFC-defined removal or SIE behavior. Permanent deletion/retention requires a declared local/provider contract.
defects.limiting_counterargument: The disposition uses the word definitive, which can be a provider-specific qualification. The cross-topic test and broader non-404/410 rule omit that qualifier; no provider evidence making every 404 definitive was supplied.
defects.discriminating_check: Distinguish 500/502/503/504, network failure, 401/403, 429, temporary/processing 404 and a provider-confirmed removal/410. Assert the chosen independent display, retry and retention responses plus SIE age/permission bounds.

defects.title: A MediaWiki parser-cache TTL is attributed to mod_tile expiry
defects.defect_identity: Keyword presence is promoted into a tile-specific numeric precedent despite a different subject and authority layer.
defects.source_facts: The captured rendering-wiki HTML places Cache expiry:86400 and Reduced expiry:false inside the NewPP parser-cache report; its other 86400 occurrence is parser-cache metadata. The page contains no mod_tile name. The mod_tile README supplies configurable expiry heuristics but no one-day value.
defects.materiality: The sole asserted numeric tile precedent for retention is absent. This is a consequential source-attribution error even though the final also says quotas are unresolved and the precedent is nonnormative. Hashes and grep counts cannot establish this semantic claim.
defects.inference: 86400 seconds equals one day, but the fact concerns caching the wiki page. The correct bounded negative is that these captured documents supply no tile one-day retention precedent.
defects.limiting_counterargument: No chosen quota directly derives from the number. Severity is therefore medium rather than claiming a demonstrated shipped quota failure.
defects.discriminating_check: Bind each numeric value to its surrounding authored/configuration subject and authority. The parser comment and metadata must be rejected as tile-policy evidence; any later actual mod_tile config capture needs its own version and locator.
